Subject: Re: Evaluation kickoff — retention & escrow questions

Elena — thanks, all clear. Quick answers up front and a proposed acceptance pathway below.

Short answers:
- SOC 2: most recent Type II report completed 2026-11-12; we can provide the full attestation under NDA.
- SIG/CAIQ: we maintain an up-to-date SIG-lite matrix; I'll attach our evidence index and a populated CAIQ excerpt for the controls you flagged.
- DPA / retention: Redwood supports configurable retention tiers. Standard options: 30d (ephemeral), 90d (short-term), 365d (standard), and custom enterprise windows with contract carveouts. Regulatory holds (e.g., 7 years) are handled via retained-archive with agreed scope — requires a limited addendum and minimum enterprise plan.

Proposed acceptance gates (MAP highlights):
1) Security evidence: SOC 2 attestation + SIG-lite matrix + evidence index (we deliver in secure folder).
2) Contract: signed DPA with retention annex (we can accept regulatory hold language but will need scope + volume limit).
3) Operational: data residency confirmation (EU-only option available for specific tenants).
4) Escrow: optional key escrow / data escrow — we support partner-managed escrow or an industry escrow (cost + timeline noted below).

Timeline proposal:
- Tue 4/27: Redwood shares evidence bundle (secure Drive) + CAIQ excerpt.
- Wed 4/28: Procurement provides DPA redlines; Redwood responses by EOD Thu 4/29.
- Mon 5/3: Signatures and handoff to onboarding for staging.

I'll attach the evidence index (redwood-evidence-index.pdf) and draft MAP (MAP-final-20270428.xlsx) if that helps. If procurement has a hard requirement around escrow, indicate whether it is key escrow or full data escrow — both are possible but differ materially on cost and SLA.

Thanks — copying Kim and Jordan for DPA escrow feasibility + timeline.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 27 Apr 2027 13:08:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Evaluation kickoff — retention & escrow questions (procurement asks)

Kim / Jordan — forwarding Palisade's asks. Summary of decisions we need today:
- Can we accept a DPA retention carveout that allows individual records to be retained up to 7 years for regulatory holds? If yes, what carrier-level constraints (storage, searchability) do we need to call out?
- Escrow: procurement is likely to ask for vendor escrow. Options we can offer: (A) key escrow for encryption keys (Redwood-managed HSM, with escrow to a neutral custodian), (B) full data escrow (periodic archive snapshots delivered to escrow custodian). Cost and timeline differ — key escrow is faster to stand up.

My recommended position: accept regulatory hold up to 7 years but require (1) scoped list of record types, (2) volume ceilings, and (3) reimbursement for extended storage beyond baseline. For escrow, offer key escrow as standard enterprise option; full data escrow possible with 30–45 day lead time + escrow fee.

Can you confirm compliance/legal language we should propose for the DPA annex? I want to reply to procurement with concrete phrasing this afternoon.

Onward — H.

Elena / team — forwarding final artifacts and next steps. Deliverables attached and notes below.

Deliverables (shared to secure Drive):
- redwood-evidence-index.pdf (SOC 2 attestation reference + SIG-lite excerpt)
- MAP-final-20270428.xlsx (mutual action plan with milestone dates)
- Draft DPA Annex (in Drive as DPA-Annex-Redwood.docx) — includes retention annex with scoped regulatory hold wording and a template escrow clause.

Key points / our positions:
- SOC 2: Auditor = Northbridge LLP; no exceptions in 2026 Type II report. We'll provide the full report under NDA (Drive folder access requested).
- Retention: Redwood will accept regulatory hold up to 7 years for scoped record classes (commercial lending, dispute records) provided Palisade: (a) lists record types, (b) commits to an upper volume (TB) estimate, and (c) accepts a pass-through storage fee if retention exceeds baseline. Language in the annex reflects that approach.
- Escrow: we propose key escrow by default (HSM-backed keys) with multi-party authorization (Redwood + escrow custodian + Palisade ops). Full data escrow is available as an add-on (snapshot cadence, 90-day retention in escrow) — estimated 30–45 day setup and one-time escrow fee in the draft annex.

Next steps (MAP milestones):
- Thu 4/29 EOD: Palisade legal to deliver DPA redlines / confirm scoped retention list.
- Mon 5/3: Redwood to finalize DPA annex and upload signed doc for signatures.
- Mon 5/10: Final evidence walkthrough and onboarding scheduling.

If that aligns, I'll ask legal to circulate a DocuSign for the DPA annex once redlines come back. Thanks for keeping this tight; happy to hop on a short call if any of legal's redline language needs live negotiation.
